- [src/gfx/view_param.h](src/gfx/view_param.h)

</details>



This document covers VIAMD's camera system, which provides 3D navigation and view control for molecular visualization. The system includes trackball controls, projection matrix generation, camera animation, and automatic view computation.

For information about the rendering pipeline that uses these camera parameters, see [Rendering Pipeline and Post-Processing](#3.1). For details about volume rendering view calculations, see [Volume Rendering System](#3.2).

## Camera Data Structure and Core Components

The camera system is built around the `Camera` struct and related view parameter structures that manage 3D scene navigation and projection.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Camera Structure"
        Camera["Camera"]
        Camera --> position["vec3_t position"]
        Camera --> orientation["quat_t orientation"]
        Camera --> fov_y["float fov_y"]
        Camera --> near_plane["float near_plane"]
        Camera --> far_plane["float far_plane"]
        Camera --> focus_distance["float focus_distance"]
    end

    subgraph "View Parameter Block"
        ViewParam["ViewParam"]
        ViewParam --> matrix_curr["matrix.curr.view/proj/norm"]
        ViewParam --> matrix_prev["matrix.prev.*"]
        ViewParam --> matrix_inv["matrix.inv.*"]
        ViewParam --> jitter["jitter.curr/prev"]
        ViewParam --> clip_planes["clip_planes.near/far"]
        ViewParam --> resolution["vec2_t resolution"]
    end

    subgraph "Matrix Generation Functions"
        camera_world_to_view_matrix["camera_world_to_view_matrix()"]
        camera_view_to_world_matrix["camera_view_to_world_matrix()"]
        camera_perspective_projection_matrix["camera_perspective_projection_matrix()"]
        camera_inverse_perspective_projection_matrix["camera_inverse_perspective_projection_matrix()"]
    end

    Camera --> camera_world_to_view_matrix
    Camera --> camera_view_to_world_matrix
    Camera --> camera_perspective_projection_matrix
    Camera --> camera_inverse_perspective_projection_matrix

    matrix_curr --> ViewParam_output["Shader Uniforms"]
    matrix_prev --> ViewParam_output
    matrix_inv --> ViewParam_output
```

The `Camera` struct stores the fundamental view parameters including position in world space, orientation as a quaternion, field of view, clipping planes, and focus distance for trackball controls. The `ViewParam` structure packages the computed matrices and temporal information needed by shaders.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/camera_utils.h:1-32](), [src/gfx/view_param.h:5-31]()

## Matrix Generation System

The camera system provides comprehensive matrix generation functions for transforming between coordinate spaces and handling projection with optional sub-pixel jittering for temporal anti-aliasing.

| Function | Purpose | Parameters |
|----------|---------|------------|
| `camera_world_to_view_matrix` | World to camera space transform | `Camera` struct |
| `camera_view_to_world_matrix` | Camera to world space transform | `Camera` struct |
| `camera_perspective_projection_matrix` | Standard perspective projection | `Camera`, aspect ratio |
| `camera_perspective_projection_matrix` (overload) | Jittered perspective projection | `Camera`, width, height, texel offsets |
| `camera_inverse_perspective_projection_matrix` | Inverse projection matrices | Same as above |
| `camera_orthographic_projection_matrix` | Orthographic projections | Left, right, bottom, top bounds |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Matrix Generation Pipeline"
        Camera_Input["Camera Input"]
        Camera_Input --> view_matrix["camera_world_to_view_matrix()"]
        Camera_Input --> projection_matrix["camera_perspective_projection_matrix()"]
        
        view_matrix --> ViewMatrix["mat4_t view"]
        projection_matrix --> ProjMatrix["mat4_t proj"]
        
        subgraph "Jitter Support"
            texel_offset_x["float texel_offset_x"]
            texel_offset_y["float texel_offset_y"]
            width["int width"]
            height["int height"]
        end
        
        texel_offset_x --> projection_extents["projection_extents()"]
        texel_offset_y --> projection_extents
        width --> projection_extents
        height --> projection_extents
        projection_extents --> mat4_frustum["mat4_frustum()"]
        
        ViewMatrix --> ViewParam_Block["ViewParam.matrix.curr"]
        ProjMatrix --> ViewParam_Block
    end
```

The matrix generation system supports both standard and jittered projection matrices. Jittering enables temporal anti-aliasing by sub-pixel offsets computed through the `projection_extents` helper function.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/camera_utils.cpp:21-81](), [src/gfx/camera_utils.h:93-106]()

## Trackball Control System

The trackball controller provides intuitive 3D navigation through rotation, panning, and dollying operations. The system maintains a focus point and rotates around it while supporting smooth distance-based scaling.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Trackball Controller Components"
        TrackballControllerInput["TrackballControllerInput"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> rotate_button["bool rotate_button"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> pan_button["bool pan_button"] 
        TrackballControllerInput --> dolly_button["bool dolly_button"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> dolly_delta["float dolly_delta"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> mouse_coord_prev["vec2_t mouse_coord_prev"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> mouse_coord_curr["vec2_t mouse_coord_curr"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> screen_size["vec2_t screen_size"]
        TrackballControllerInput --> fov_y["float fov_y"]
    end

    subgraph "Trackball Parameters"
        TrackballControllerParam["TrackballControllerParam"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> pan_scale["float pan_scale"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> pan_exponent["float pan_exponent"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> dolly_drag_scale["float dolly_drag_scale"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> dolly_drag_exponent["float dolly_drag_exponent"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> min_distance["float min_distance"]
        TrackballControllerParam --> max_distance["float max_distance"]
    end

    subgraph "Control Operations"
        camera_controller_trackball["camera_controller_trackball()"]
        trackball_func["trackball()"]
        project_to_sphere["project_to_sphere()"]
    end

    TrackballControllerInput --> camera_controller_trackball
    TrackballControllerParam --> camera_controller_trackball
    camera_controller_trackball --> trackball_func
    trackball_func --> project_to_sphere

    subgraph "Output"
        position_out["vec3_t* position"]
        orientation_out["quat_t* orientation"] 
        distance_out["float* distance"]
    end

    camera_controller_trackball --> position_out
    camera_controller_trackball --> orientation_out
    camera_controller_trackball --> distance_out
```

The trackball implementation uses virtual sphere projection to convert 2D mouse movements into 3D rotations. The `project_to_sphere` function maps screen coordinates to a virtual trackball sphere, while the `trackball` function computes the rotation quaternion between two sphere points.

### Trackball Operation Modes

| Operation | Trigger | Behavior |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| **Rotation** | `rotate_button` + mouse drag | Rotates around focus point using virtual sphere |
| **Panning** | `pan_button` + mouse drag | Translates camera parallel to view plane |
| **Dollying** | `dolly_button` + mouse drag or `dolly_delta` | Moves camera toward/away from focus point |

The controller supports configurable scaling parameters with exponential distance relationships, allowing smooth navigation across different molecular scales.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/camera_utils.cpp:96-235](), [src/gfx/camera_utils.h:23-86]()

## Camera Animation and Interpolation

The camera system provides smooth transitions between view states through quaternion-based interpolation that maintains focus point relationships and handles precision issues in long animations.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Animation Functions"
        camera_interpolate_look_at["camera_interpolate_look_at()"]
        camera_animate["camera_animate()"]
        highp_quat_vec3_mul["highp_quat_vec3_mul()"]
    end

    subgraph "Input State"
        in_pos["vec3_t in_pos[2]"]
        in_ori["quat_t in_ori[2]"]
        in_dist["float in_dist[2]"]
        t_param["double t"]
    end

    subgraph "Output State"
        out_pos["vec3_t* out_pos"]
        out_ori["quat_t* out_ori"]
        out_dist["float* out_dist"]
    end

    subgraph "Animation Pipeline"
        quat_slerp["quat_slerp()"]
        lerp_func["lerp()"]
        epsilon_check["Precision Epsilon Checks"]
    end

    in_pos --> camera_interpolate_look_at
    in_ori --> camera_interpolate_look_at
    in_dist --> camera_interpolate_look_at
    t_param --> camera_interpolate_look_at

    camera_interpolate_look_at --> quat_slerp
    camera_interpolate_look_at --> lerp_func
    camera_interpolate_look_at --> epsilon_check
    camera_interpolate_look_at --> highp_quat_vec3_mul

    camera_interpolate_look_at --> out_pos
    camera_interpolate_look_at --> out_ori
    camera_interpolate_look_at --> out_dist

    subgraph "High-Level Animation"
        Camera_input["Camera* camera"]
        target_ori["quat_t target_ori"]
        target_pos["vec3_t target_pos"] 
        target_dist["float target_dist"]
        dt["double dt"]
    end

    Camera_input --> camera_animate
    target_ori --> camera_animate
    target_pos --> camera_animate
    target_dist --> camera_animate
    dt --> camera_animate

    camera_animate --> camera_interpolate_look_at
```

The interpolation system maintains focus point consistency by computing implicit look-at positions and interpolating them separately from camera positions. This prevents drift during long animations. The `highp_quat_vec3_mul` function provides double-precision quaternion-vector multiplication to combat floating-point errors.

### Animation Precision Handling

The system employs epsilon-based comparisons to avoid unnecessary computations:

- **Quaternion epsilon**: `1.0e-7` for orientation similarity
- **Position epsilon**: `1.0e-7` for spatial proximity  
- **Distance epsilon**: `1.0e-7` for focus distance similarity

When values are within epsilon thresholds, the system uses the target value directly instead of interpolating, preventing numerical drift.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/camera_utils.cpp:134-286](), [src/gfx/camera_utils.h:91-115]()

## Automatic View Computation

The system provides automatic camera positioning through the `camera_compute_optimal_view` function, which analyzes molecular geometry to compute optimal viewing angles and distances.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Optimal View Computation"
        input_basis["mat3_t in_basis"]
        input_min_ext["vec3_t in_min_ext"]
        input_max_ext["vec3_t in_max_ext"]
        distance_scale["float distance_scale"]
    end

    subgraph "Analysis Pipeline"
        compute_extents["Extent Analysis"]
        anisotropy_check["Anisotropy Check"]
        axis_sorting["Axis Sorting by Length"]
        direction_computation["Direction Computation"]
    end

    subgraph "View Direction Calculation"
        right_axis["right = in_basis[l[0]]"]
        up_axis["up = in_basis[l[1]]"]
        out_axis["out = in_basis[l[2]]"]
        view_dir["dir = normalize(right*0.6 + up*0.5 + out*1.0)"]
    end

    subgraph "Camera Positioning"
        center_calc["cen = basis * ((min_ext + max_ext) * 0.5)"]
        position_calc["pos = cen + dir * len * distance_scale"]
        orientation_calc["ori = quat_from_mat4(mat4_look_at(...))"]
    end

    input_basis --> compute_extents
    input_min_ext --> compute_extents
    input_max_ext --> compute_extents
    compute_extents --> anisotropy_check
    anisotropy_check --> axis_sorting
    axis_sorting --> direction_computation

    direction_computation --> right_axis
    direction_computation --> up_axis
    direction_computation --> out_axis
    right_axis --> view_dir
    up_axis --> view_dir
    out_axis --> view_dir

    view_dir --> center_calc
    view_dir --> position_calc
    center_calc --> position_calc
    position_calc --> orientation_calc

    distance_scale --> position_calc
```

The optimal view algorithm performs several steps:

1. **Extent Analysis**: Computes bounding box dimensions and determines anisotropy ratio
2. **Axis Sorting**: Orders coordinate axes by extent length when anisotropy > 1.1
3. **Direction Computation**: Creates viewing direction using weighted axis combination
4. **Camera Positioning**: Places camera at computed distance along viewing direction

The algorithm prioritizes views that show the longest molecular axis horizontally and positions the camera at an optimal distance based on the molecular size.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/camera_utils.cpp:237-271](), [src/gfx/camera_utils.h:113]()

## Integration with Rendering Pipeline

The camera system interfaces with the rendering pipeline through the `ViewParam` structure, which packages current and previous frame matrices for temporal effects.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Camera System Output"
        Camera_State["Camera State"]
        view_matrix_current["Current View Matrix"]
        proj_matrix_current["Current Projection Matrix"]
        view_matrix_previous["Previous View Matrix"]
        proj_matrix_previous["Previous Projection Matrix"]
    end

    subgraph "ViewParam Structure"
        ViewParam_curr["matrix.curr.*"]
        ViewParam_prev["matrix.prev.*"]
        ViewParam_inv["matrix.inv.*"]
        ViewParam_jitter["jitter.curr/prev"]
    end

    subgraph "Shader Uniforms"
        uniform_view["uniform mat4 u_view"]
        uniform_proj["uniform mat4 u_proj"]
        uniform_norm["uniform mat4 u_norm"]
        uniform_jitter["uniform vec2 u_jitter"]
    end

    Camera_State --> view_matrix_current
    Camera_State --> proj_matrix_current
    Camera_State --> view_matrix_previous
    Camera_State --> proj_matrix_previous

    view_matrix_current --> ViewParam_curr
    proj_matrix_current --> ViewParam_curr
    view_matrix_previous --> ViewParam_prev
    proj_matrix_previous --> ViewParam_prev

    ViewParam_curr --> uniform_view
    ViewParam_curr --> uniform_proj
    ViewParam_curr --> uniform_norm
    ViewParam_jitter --> uniform_jitter
```

The `ViewParam` structure maintains both current and previous frame matrices to support temporal rendering effects like motion blur and temporal anti-aliasing. The inverse matrices enable efficient screen-space to world-space transformations in shaders.

**Sources**: [src/gfx/view_param.h:5-31]()

# GLSL Shaders

This document covers the GLSL shader system in VIAMD, including volume rendering, post-processing effects, and deferred rendering shaders. The shaders implement advanced rendering techniques for molecular visualization, including direct volume rendering, isosurface extraction, temporal anti-aliasing, depth of field, and physically-based shading.

For information about the overall rendering pipeline architecture, see [Rendering Pipeline and Post-Processing](#3.1). For volume rendering system details, see [Volume Rendering System](#3.2).

## Shader Pipeline Overview

VIAMD's shader system implements a multi-stage rendering pipeline that processes molecular data through volume rendering, deferred shading, and post-processing effects.

**Shader Pipeline Architecture**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Volume Rendering Stage"
        VolumeEntry["u_tex_entry<br/>Entry Position Buffer"]
        VolumeExit["u_tex_exit<br/>Exit Position Buffer"]
        VolumeTexture["u_tex_volume<br/>3D Volume Data"]
        TransferFunc["u_tex_tf<br/>Transfer Function"]
        
        RaycastShader["raycaster.frag<br/>Volume Raycasting"]
        
        VolumeEntry --> RaycastShader
        VolumeExit --> RaycastShader
        VolumeTexture --> RaycastShader
        TransferFunc --> RaycastShader
    end
    
    subgraph "Deferred Rendering Stage"
        GBufferColor["G-Buffer Color"]
        GBufferNormal["G-Buffer Normal"]
        GBufferDepth["G-Buffer Depth"]
        
        DeferredShader["compose_deferred.frag<br/>PBR Composition"]
        
        GBufferColor --> DeferredShader
        GBufferNormal --> DeferredShader
        GBufferDepth --> DeferredShader
    end
    
    subgraph "Post-Processing Stage"
        ColorBuffer["Color Buffer"]
        DepthBuffer["Depth Buffer"]
        VelocityBuffer["Velocity Buffer"]
        
        TemporalShader["temporal.frag<br/>Temporal Anti-aliasing"]
        DOFShader["dof.frag<br/>Depth of Field"]
        
        ColorBuffer --> TemporalShader
        DepthBuffer --> TemporalShader
        VelocityBuffer --> TemporalShader
        
        TemporalShader --> DOFShader
        DepthBuffer --> DOFShader
    end
    
    RaycastShader --> GBufferColor
    RaycastShader --> GBufferNormal
    RaycastShader --> GBufferDepth
    
    DeferredShader --> ColorBuffer
    
    DOFShader --> FinalOutput["Final Rendered Image"]
    
    style RaycastShader fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style DeferredShader fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style TemporalShader fill:#bfb,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style DOFShader fill:#ffb,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

Sources: [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag](), [src/shaders/compose_deferred.frag](), [src/shaders/temporal.frag](), [src/shaders/dof/dof.frag]()

## Volume Rendering Shaders

The volume rendering system uses GPU-based raycasting to visualize 3D molecular data, supporting both direct volume rendering and isosurface extraction.

### Volume Raycaster

The primary volume rendering shader `raycaster.frag` implements a comprehensive raycasting algorithm with support for multiple rendering modes.

**Volume Raycasting Implementation**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Raycasting Setup"
        EntryExit["Entry/Exit Position Calculation<br/>gl_FragCoord → entryPos, exitPos"]
        RaySetup["Ray Setup<br/>ori = entryPos<br/>dir = normalize(exitPos - entryPos)"]
        Sampling["Sampling Rate Calculation<br/>tIncr = tEnd / (samplingRate * samples)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ray Marching Loop"
        SamplePos["Sample Position<br/>samplePos = entryPos + t * dir"]
        VoxelSample["Volume Sampling<br/>getVoxel(samplePos)"]
        
        IsoCheck["Isosurface Check<br/>drawIsosurfaces()"]
        DVRClassify["DVR Classification<br/>classify(density)"]
        Compositing["Alpha Compositing<br/>compositing(result, srcColor)"]
        
        ERT["Early Ray Termination<br/>result.a > ERT_THRESHOLD"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Shading Pipeline"
        GradientCalc["Gradient Calculation<br/>getGradient(samplePos)"]
        PBRShading["PBR Shading<br/>Cook-Torrance Model"]
        Tonemap["Tone Mapping<br/>Tonemap(color)"]
    end
    
    EntryExit --> RaySetup
    RaySetup --> Sampling
    Sampling --> SamplePos
    SamplePos --> VoxelSample
    VoxelSample --> IsoCheck
    VoxelSample --> DVRClassify
    IsoCheck --> GradientCalc
    DVRClassify --> Compositing
    GradientCalc --> PBRShading
    PBRShading --> Tonemap
    Tonemap --> Compositing
    Compositing --> ERT
    ERT --> SamplePos
```

**Key Shader Functions:**

| Function | Purpose | Location |
|----------|---------|----------|
| `getVoxel(vec3)` | Sample volume texture | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:79-81]() |
| `classify(float)` | Transfer function lookup | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:83-87]() |
| `compositing(vec4, vec4, float)` | Alpha blending | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:89-94]() |
| `getGradient(vec3)` | Central difference gradient | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:96-104]() |
| `drawIsosurface(...)` | Isosurface intersection | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:213-269]() |
| `shade(vec4, vec3, vec3)` | PBR shading calculation | [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:146-191]() |

**Isosurface Parameters:**

The shader supports up to `MAX_ISOVALUE_COUNT` isosurfaces simultaneously through the `IsovalueParameters` uniform block:

```glsl
struct IsovalueParameters {
    float values[MAX_ISOVALUE_COUNT];
    vec4  colors[MAX_ISOVALUE_COUNT];
    int count;
};
```

Sources: [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:1-391]()

## Post-Processing Shaders

The post-processing pipeline applies temporal anti-aliasing and depth of field effects to improve visual quality.

### Temporal Anti-Aliasing

The `temporal.frag` shader implements temporal reprojection to reduce aliasing artifacts and provide motion blur effects.

**Temporal Reprojection Pipeline**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Current Frame"
        CurrentColor["u_tex_main<br/>Current Color"]
        CurrentDepth["u_tex_linear_depth<br/>Current Depth"]
        CurrentVel["u_tex_vel<br/>Velocity Buffer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Previous Frame"
        PrevColor["u_tex_prev<br/>Previous Color"]
        PrevJitter["u_jitter_uv.zw<br/>Previous Jitter"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Reprojection Process"
        VelDilation["sample_velocity_dilated()<br/>Velocity Dilation"]
        NeighborhoodSample["Neighborhood Sampling<br/>3x3 or 4-tap minmax"]
        ColorClamp["clip_aabb()<br/>Color Clamping"]
        TemporalBlend["Temporal Blending<br/>k_feedback calculation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Motion Blur"
        MotionSample["sample_color_motion()<br/>Motion Sampling"]
        VelTrust["Velocity Trust<br/>vel_mag based blending"]
    end
    
    CurrentColor --> NeighborhoodSample
    CurrentVel --> VelDilation
    VelDilation --> TemporalBlend
    
    PrevColor --> ColorClamp
    NeighborhoodSample --> ColorClamp
    ColorClamp --> TemporalBlend
    
    CurrentColor --> MotionSample
    MotionSample --> VelTrust
    TemporalBlend --> VelTrust
    
    VelTrust --> FinalOutput["Final Anti-aliased Color"]
```

**Color Space Options:**

The shader supports multiple color space transformations and clamping methods:

| Option | Purpose | Default |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `USE_YCOCG` | YCoCg color space processing | 0 |
| `USE_CLIPPING` | AABB clipping vs simple clamping | 1 |
| `USE_MOTION_BLUR` | Motion blur rendering | 1 |
| `MINMAX_3X3` | 3x3 neighborhood sampling | 0 |
| `MINMAX_3X3_ROUNDED` | Rounded 3x3 + 5-tap | 1 |

Sources: [src/shaders/temporal.frag:1-561]()

### Depth of Field

The `dof.frag` shader implements single-pass bokeh depth of field using golden angle spiral sampling.

**DOF Sampling Pattern**

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "DOF Parameters"
        FocusDepth["u_focus_depth<br/>Focus Distance"]
        FocusScale["u_focus_scale<br/>Focus Strength"]
        CenterDepth["Center Pixel Depth"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Circle of Confusion"
        COCCalc["get_blur_size()<br/>coc = (1/focus - 1/depth) * scale"]
        BlurRadius["Blur Radius<br/>abs(coc) * MAX_BLUR_SIZE"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Spiral Sampling"
        GoldenAngle["GOLDEN_ANGLE = 2.39996323"]
        RadiusStep["radius += RAD_SCALE/radius"]
        SamplePos["tc + vec2(cos(ang), sin(ang)) * radius"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Sample Weighting"
        DepthTest["sample_depth > center_depth"]
        COCClamp["sample_coc = min(sample_coc, center_coc*2)"]
        BlendWeight["smoothstep(radius-0.5, radius+0.5, coc)"]
    end
    
    FocusDepth --> COCCalc
    FocusScale --> COCCalc
    CenterDepth --> COCCalc
    COCCalc --> BlurRadius
    
    BlurRadius --> GoldenAngle
    GoldenAngle --> RadiusStep
    RadiusStep --> SamplePos
    
    SamplePos --> DepthTest
    DepthTest --> COCClamp
    COCClamp --> BlendWeight
```

**DOF Constants:**

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `GOLDEN_ANGLE` | 2.39996323 | Spiral sampling angle |
| `MAX_BLUR_SIZE` | 15.0 | Maximum blur radius |
| `RAD_SCALE` | 1.5 | Radius increment scale |

Sources: [src/shaders/dof/dof.frag:1-102]()

## Common Shader Utilities

Several utility functions are shared across shaders for consistent rendering quality.

### Noise Generation

All shaders use pseudo-random number generation for jittering and dithering:

```glsl
float PDnrand(vec2 n) {
    return fract(sin(dot(n.xy, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453);
}
```

### Tone Mapping

Reversible tone mapping is used in temporal anti-aliasing:

```glsl
vec3 tonemap(vec3 color) {
    return color * rcp(max3(color) + 1.0);
}

vec3 tonemap_invert(vec3 color) {
    return color * rcp(1.0 - max3(color));
}
```

### Normal Encoding/Decoding

Compact normal storage using Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection:

```glsl
vec2 encode_normal(vec3 n) {
    float p = sqrt(n.z * 8 + 8);
    return n.xy / p + 0.5;
}

vec3 decode_normal(vec2 enc) {
    vec2 fenc = enc * 4 - 2;
    float f = dot(fenc, fenc);
    float g = sqrt(1 - f / 4.0);
    vec3 n;
    n.xy = fenc * g;
    n.z = 1 - f / 2.0;
    return n;
}
```

Sources: [src/shaders/volume/raycaster.frag:332-335](), [src/shaders/temporal.frag:129-148](), [src/shaders/compose_deferred.frag:28-37]()

# Page: Analysis and Computation

# Analysis and Computation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp](src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp)

- [src/task_system.cpp](src/task_system.cpp)

- [src/viamd.h](src/viamd.h)

</details>



This document covers VIAMD's analysis and computation capabilities, including the parallel task system, molecular dynamics analysis components, and quantum chemistry integration. The analysis system provides specialized tools for protein structure analysis (Ramachandran plots), molecular shape characterization (shape space), and electronic structure visualization (VeloxChem integration).

For information about the graphics rendering pipeline, see [Graphics and Visualization Pipeline](#3). For details about the user interface components that display analysis results, see [User Interface Framework](#5).

## Analysis System Architecture

VIAMD's analysis system is built around an event-driven architecture with asynchronous task processing. The system coordinates multiple specialized analysis components through a centralized event system and executes computationally intensive work using a parallel task scheduler.

### Component Overview

```mermaid

        MAIN["Main Tasks (Main Thread)"]

        SHAPE["Shapespace Component"] 
        VLX["VeloxChem Component"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Structures"

        PROPS["DisplayProperty[]"]
        TASKS["task_system::ID handles"]
    end
    
    ES --> EH
    EH --> RAMA
    EH --> SHAPE
    EH --> VLX
    
    RAMA --> TS
    SHAPE --> TS
    VLX --> TS
    
    TS --> POOL

    RAMA --> AS

    VLX --> AS

```

### Event-Driven Component Coordination

The analysis system uses a centralized event system to coordinate between components and the main application. Each analysis component implements the `viamd::EventHandler` interface and registers itself to receive relevant events.

## Parallel Task System

The task system provides asynchronous computation capabilities through a thread pool architecture. It supports both main thread tasks (for UI updates) and worker pool tasks (for computation-intensive operations).

### Task Management Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Task Creation"
        CREATE_MAIN["create_main_task()"]
        CREATE_POOL["create_pool_task()"]
        CREATE_RANGE["create_pool_task() with RangeTask"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Storage"
        MAIN_SLOTS["main::task_data[MAX_TASKS]"]
        POOL_SLOTS["pool::task_data[MAX_TASKS]"]
        FREE_MAIN["main::free_slots queue"]
        FREE_POOL["pool::free_slots queue"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Engine" 
        TS["enki::TaskScheduler"]
        MAIN_EXEC["execute_main_task_queue()"]
        POOL_EXEC["Worker Thread Pool"]
    end
    
    CREATE_MAIN --> FREE_MAIN
    CREATE_POOL --> FREE_POOL
    CREATE_RANGE --> FREE_POOL
    
    FREE_MAIN --> MAIN_SLOTS
    FREE_POOL --> POOL_SLOTS
    
    MAIN_SLOTS --> MAIN_EXEC
    POOL_SLOTS --> POOL_EXEC
    
    MAIN_EXEC --> TS
    POOL_EXEC --> TS
```

**Sources:** [src/task_system.cpp:22-296](), [src/task_system.h:9-64]()

### Task Lifecycle and Dependencies

The task system manages task lifecycles through unique IDs and supports dependency chains between tasks:

| Task State | Description | Key Functions |
|------------|-------------|---------------|
| Created | Task allocated but not queued | `create_main_task()`, `create_pool_task()` |
| Dependent | Waiting for dependency completion | `set_task_dependency()` |
| Queued | Ready for execution | `enqueue_task()` |
| Running | Currently executing | `task_is_running()` |
| Complete | Finished execution | Automatic cleanup |

**Sources:** [src/task_system.cpp:158-296](), [src/task_system.h:29-62]()

## Ramachandran Plot Analysis

The Ramachandran component analyzes protein backbone conformation by computing phi-psi angle distributions. It generates density maps for different residue types and provides interactive visualization.

### Ramachandran Types and Processing

The system classifies residues into four Ramachandran types and processes them separately:

| Glycine | `MD_RAMACHANDRAN_TYPE_GLYCINE` | Glycine residues |
| Proline | `MD_RAMACHANDRAN_TYPE_PROLINE` | Proline residues |

## Shape Space Analysis

The shape space component characterizes molecular shapes using principal moment analysis, projecting structures onto a triangular shape space defined by linear, planar, and spherical extremes.

### Shape Space Computation Pipeline


**Sources:** [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:360-428](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:394-421]()

### Shape Weight Calculation

The system computes three shape descriptors that sum to 1.0:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Shape Triangle Vertices"
        LIN["Linear (0,0)"]
        PLA["Planar (1,0)"] 
        ISO["Spherical (0.5, 0.866)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Weight Computation"
        MOMENTS["Principal moments λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃"]
        W_LIN["w_linear = (λ₁-λ₂)/(λ₁+λ₂+λ₃)"]
        W_PLA["w_planar = 2(λ₂-λ₃)/(λ₁+λ₂+λ₃)"]
        W_ISO["w_spherical = 3λ₃/(λ₁+λ₂+λ₃)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Coordinates"
        COORD["coord = w_lin*LIN + w_pla*PLA + w_iso*ISO"]
    end
    
    MOMENTS --> W_LIN
    MOMENTS --> W_PLA  
    MOMENTS --> W_ISO
    
    W_LIN --> COORD
    W_PLA --> COORD
    W_ISO --> COORD
    
    LIN --> COORD
    PLA --> COORD
    ISO --> COORD
```

**Sources:** [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:394-422]()

# Page: Task System and Parallel Processing

# Task System and Parallel Processing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp](src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp)
- [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp](src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp)
- [src/event.h](src/event.h)
- [src/task_system.cpp](src/task_system.cpp)
- [src/task_system.h](src/task_system.h)

</details>



This document covers VIAMD's task system for parallel processing and asynchronous computation. The system provides a high-level interface for creating and managing background tasks, enabling compute-intensive operations like density calculations and molecular analysis to be performed without blocking the main thread.

For information about the event system that coordinates communication between components, see [Event System](#2.3). For details about specific analysis components that use the task system, see [Ramachandran Plot Analysis](#4.2) and [Shape Space Analysis](#4.3).

## Architecture Overview

VIAMD's task system is built on top of the enkiTS task scheduler, providing a simplified interface for creating, scheduling, and managing parallel tasks. The system supports both main thread execution and worker thread pools.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Task System Interface"
        API["task_system namespace<br/>src/task_system.h"]
        IMPL["Task Implementation<br/>src/task_system.cpp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Types"
        MAIN_TASK["MainTask<br/>IPinnedTask"]
        ASYNC_TASK["AsyncTask<br/>ITaskSet"]
        COMPLETION["CompletionActionFreePoolSlot<br/>ICompletable"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Storage and Management"
        MAIN_SLOTS["main::task_data[MAX_TASKS]<br/>MainTask array"]
        POOL_SLOTS["pool::task_data[MAX_TASKS]<br/>AsyncTask array"]
        FREE_MAIN["main::free_slots<br/>AtomicQueue"]
        FREE_POOL["pool::free_slots<br/>AtomicQueue"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        ENKITS["enki::TaskScheduler<br/>ext/enkiTS"]
        ATOMIC_Q["atomic_queue::AtomicQueue<br/>ext/atomic_queue"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Client Components"
        RAMA["Ramachandran<br/>density computation"]
        SHAPE["Shapespace<br/>shape analysis"]
        OTHER["Other Analysis<br/>Components"]
    end
    
    API --> IMPL
    IMPL --> MAIN_TASK
    IMPL --> ASYNC_TASK
    IMPL --> COMPLETION
    
    MAIN_TASK --> MAIN_SLOTS
    ASYNC_TASK --> POOL_SLOTS
    MAIN_SLOTS --> FREE_MAIN
    POOL_SLOTS --> FREE_POOL
    
    IMPL --> ENKITS
    FREE_MAIN --> ATOMIC_Q
    FREE_POOL --> ATOMIC_Q
    
    RAMA --> API
    SHAPE --> API
    OTHER --> API
```

Sources: [src/task_system.h](), [src/task_system.cpp:1-296](), [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:622-684](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-430]()

## Task Types and Lifecycle

The task system supports two primary task types with distinct execution models and lifecycle management.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Created
    
    state "Task Creation" as Created {
        [*] --> MainTaskCreated: create_main_task()
        [*] --> PoolTaskCreated: create_pool_task()
        
        MainTaskCreated --> SlotAllocated: get main::free_slot
        PoolTaskCreated --> SlotAllocated: get pool::free_slot
        
        SlotAllocated --> IDGenerated: generate_id(slot_idx)
        IDGenerated --> TaskInitialized: PLACEMENT_NEW
    }
    
    Created --> DependencySet: set_task_dependency()
    Created --> Enqueued: enqueue_task()
    DependencySet --> Enqueued: enqueue_task()
    
    state "Task Execution" as Executing {
        Enqueued --> MainQueue: MainTask
        Enqueued --> PoolQueue: AsyncTask
        
        MainQueue --> MainExecution: execute_main_task_queue()
        PoolQueue --> PoolExecution: TaskScheduler.AddTaskSetToPipe()
        
        MainExecution --> [*]: Execute() + free slot
        PoolExecution --> [*]: ExecuteRange() + completion action
    }
    
    Enqueued --> Executing
    Executing --> [*]
    
    state "Task Control" as Control {
        Executing --> Interrupted: task_interrupt()
        Interrupted --> [*]: completion with interrupt flag
    }
```

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:158-179](), [src/task_system.cpp:182-206](), [src/task_system.cpp:209-211](), [src/task_system.cpp:279-294]()

## Core Task Classes

### AsyncTask Class

The `AsyncTask` class extends `enki::ITaskSet` and handles parallel execution on worker threads:

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `m_set_func` | `RangeTask` | Function executed across range |
| `m_func` | `Task` | Single function execution |
| `m_set_size` | `uint32_t` | Total work units |
| `m_grain_size` | `uint32_t` | Work units per execution |
| `m_set_complete` | `atomic_uint32_t` | Completed work tracking |
| `m_interrupt` | `atomic_bool` | Interruption flag |
| `m_completion_action` | `CompletionActionFreePoolSlot` | Cleanup handler |

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:54-104]()

### MainTask Class

The `MainTask` class extends `enki::IPinnedTask` for main thread execution:

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `m_function` | `Task` | Function to execute |
| `m_dependency` | `enki::Dependency` | Task dependency |
| `m_label` | `str_t` | Debug label |
| `m_id` | `ID` | Unique task identifier |

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:106-125]()

## Task ID Management

Task IDs are generated using a combination of timestamp and slot index to ensure uniqueness:

```cpp
// ID generation combines timestamp and slot index
static inline ID generate_id(uint32_t slot_idx) {
    return (md_time_current() << 8) | (slot_idx & (MAX_TASKS - 1));
}

static inline uint32_t get_slot_idx(ID id) {
    return (uint32_t)(id & (MAX_TASKS - 1));
}
```

The system maintains fixed-size arrays for task storage with lock-free slot allocation using `atomic_queue::AtomicQueue`.

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:27-33](), [src/task_system.cpp:36-41]()

## Task Dependencies and Scheduling

Tasks can have dependencies that must complete before execution begins. The dependency system uses enkiTS's built-in dependency management:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Dependency Chain"
        TASK_A["Task A<br/>ID: 12345"]
        TASK_B["Task B<br/>ID: 12346"] 
        TASK_C["Task C<br/>ID: 12347"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scheduling Flow"
        CREATE_A["create_pool_task()<br/>returns ID A"]
        CREATE_B["create_pool_task()<br/>returns ID B"]
        SET_DEP["set_task_dependency(B, A)<br/>B depends on A"]
        ENQUEUE_A["enqueue_task(A)"]
        ENQUEUE_B["enqueue_task(B)"]
        EXECUTE["TaskScheduler execution"]
    end
    
    CREATE_A --> TASK_A
    CREATE_B --> TASK_B
    SET_DEP --> TASK_B
    ENQUEUE_A --> EXECUTE
    ENQUEUE_B --> EXECUTE
    TASK_A --> TASK_B: "completion triggers"
    TASK_B --> TASK_C: "can depend on B"
```

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:238-251](), [src/task_system.h:33-37]()

## Usage Patterns in VIAMD Components

### Ramachandran Analysis

The Ramachandran component uses the task system for density computation across trajectory frames:

```cpp
// Create range task for density computation
compute_density_full = rama_rep_compute_density(
    &rama_data.full, 
    state.trajectory_data.backbone_angles.data, 
    frame_beg, frame_end, frame_stride
);
```

The task iterates over frames in parallel, computing phi/psi angle densities for protein backbone analysis.

The ShapeSpace component creates range tasks for molecular shape analysis:

```cpp
evaluate_task = task_system::create_pool_task(
    STR_LIT("Eval Shape Space"), 
    (uint32_t)num_frames, 
    [shapespace = this](uint32_t range_beg, uint32_t range_end, uint32_t thread_num) {
        // Compute shape weights for frame range
        for (uint32_t frame_idx = range_beg; frame_idx < range_end; ++frame_idx) {
            // Load trajectory frame
            // Compute covariance matrix
            // Calculate shape weights
        }
    }
);
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-425]()

## Thread Safety and Performance

### Lock-Free Slot Management

The task system uses lock-free atomic queues for slot allocation, minimizing contention between threads:

```cpp
// Lock-free slot allocation
namespace main {
    static atomic_queue::AtomicQueue<uint32_t, MAX_TASKS, 0xFFFFFFFF> free_slots;
}
namespace pool {
    static atomic_queue::AtomicQueue<uint32_t, MAX_TASKS, 0xFFFFFFFF> free_slots;
}
```

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:35-41]()

### Task Interruption

Tasks can be interrupted for responsive cancellation of long-running operations:

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `task_interrupt(ID)` | Signal interruption flag |
| `task_interrupt_and_wait_for(ID)` | Interrupt and block until completion |
| `pool_interrupt_running_tasks()` | Interrupt all running tasks |

Tasks check the `m_interrupt` flag during execution to enable cooperative cancellation.

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:279-294](), [src/task_system.cpp:226-232]()

### Progress Tracking

Range tasks provide progress information through completion counters:

```cpp
float task_fraction_complete(ID id) {
    uint32_t slot_idx = get_slot_idx(id);
    AsyncTask* Task = &pool::task_data[slot_idx];
    return Task->m_id == id ? 
        (float)Task->m_set_complete / (float)Task->m_SetSize : 0.f;
}
```

Sources: [src/task_system.cpp:265-269]()

## API Reference

### Task Creation Functions

| Function | Purpose | Returns |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `create_main_task(label, func)` | Create main thread task | Task ID |
| `create_pool_task(label, func)` | Create worker thread task | Task ID |
| `create_pool_task(label, range_size, func, grain_size)` | Create range task | Task ID |

### Task Control Functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `enqueue_task(ID)` | Queue task for execution |
| `set_task_dependency(task_id, dep_id)` | Set task dependency |
| `execute_main_task_queue()` | Execute main thread tasks |
| `pool_wait_for_completion()` | Wait for all pool tasks |

### Task Query Functions

| Function | Returns |
|----------|---------|
| `task_is_running(ID)` | `bool` - task running status |
| `task_label(ID)` | `str_t` - task debug label |
| `task_fraction_complete(ID)` | `float` - completion percentage |
| `pool_num_threads()` | `size_t` - worker thread count |

Sources: [src/task_system.h:22-62]()

# Page: Ramachandran Plot Analysis

# Ramachandran Plot Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [src/task_system.h](src/task_system.h)

## Purpose and Scope

The Ramachandran Plot Analysis system provides interactive visualization and analysis of protein backbone dihedral angles (phi and psi) in molecular dynamics trajectories. This component generates density plots, reference comparisons, and enables interactive selection of protein conformations through 2D plot interfaces.

This system is part of the broader analysis framework and integrates with the parallel task system for computational performance. For general task scheduling and parallel processing, see [Task System and Parallel Processing](#4.1). For molecular visualization components, see [Molecular Data Structures and Display](#2.4).

```cpp
struct rama_rep_t {
    uint32_t map_tex[4];  // Colormap textures for 4 types
    uint32_t iso_tex[4];  // Isoline textures for 4 types  
    float    den_sum[4];  // Density normalization values
    uint32_t den_tex;     // Combined 4-channel density texture
};
```

## Parallel Density Computation

### Task System Integration

The system leverages the task system for parallel density computation across trajectory frames:

```cpp
compute_density_full = rama_rep_compute_density(
    &rama_data.full, 
    state.trajectory_data.backbone_angles.data, 
    frame_beg, frame_end, frame_stride
);
```

This creates a `task_system::ID` that can be monitored, interrupted, and synchronized.

**Sources:** [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:664](), [src/task_system.h:29-31]()

### Density Computation Algorithm

| Phase | Function | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Classification | Type assignment | Assigns residues to General/Glycine/Proline/Pre-Proline |
| Accumulation | Angle binning | Accumulates phi/psi angles into 180x180 density grid |
| Smoothing | `blur_density_gaussian()` | Applies Gaussian blur for smooth visualization |
| Normalization | Density scaling | Normalizes density values for texture upload |

**Sources:** [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:369-388](), [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:286-367]()

## GPU Rendering Pipeline

### Shader-Based Visualization

The system uses two specialized fragment shaders for different visualization modes:

#### Colormap Shader (`f_shader_map_src`)
- Maps density values to colors using configurable colormaps
- Supports 4 ramachandran types in single pass
- Handles viewport transformation and texture sampling

#### Isoline Shader (`f_shader_iso_src`)
- Generates contour lines at specified density levels
- Anti-aliased line rendering using `fwidth()` derivatives
- Supports both filled regions and contour outlines

**Sources:** [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:91-131](), [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp:133-195]()

## Performance Optimization

### Memory Management

```cpp
arena = md_arena_allocator_create(state.allocator.persistent, MEGABYTES(1));
```

### Computational Optimizations

| Technique | Implementation | Benefit |
|-----------|----------------|---------|
| Block transpose | `transpose()` function | Cache-efficient blur operations |
| Box filter approximation | `boxes_for_gauss()` | Fast Gaussian blur via separable box filters |
| Texture caching | Fingerprint comparison | Avoid redundant computation |
| Task interruption | `task_interrupt()` | Responsive UI during computation |

# Page: Shape Space Analysis

# Shape Space Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp](src/components/ramachandran/ramachandran.cpp)
- [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp](src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp)
- [src/event.h](src/event.h)
- [src/task_system.cpp](src/task_system.cpp)
- [src/task_system.h](src/task_system.h)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Shape Space Analysis component provides real-time computation and visualization of molecular shape descriptors for trajectory analysis. It computes principal moments of inertia for selected atoms across trajectory frames and plots the resulting shape weights in a triangular coordinate system that represents the spectrum from linear to planar to spherical molecular conformations.

For general analysis and computation framework information, see [Analysis and Computation](#4). For parallel processing details used by this component, see [Task System and Parallel Processing](#4.1).

## Overview

The Shape Space Analysis system analyzes molecular shapes by computing three normalized shape weights (linear, planar, and isotropic) based on the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of atomic coordinates. These weights are visualized in a triangular plot where the vertices represent idealized linear, planar, and spherical shapes.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Shape Space Analysis Workflow"
        INPUT[User Filter Expression] --> PARSE[md_filter_evaluate]
        PARSE --> BITFIELDS[Atom Selection Bitfields]
        BITFIELDS --> TASK[Parallel Frame Processing]
        TASK --> COM[Center of Mass Computation]
        COM --> COV[Covariance Matrix Calculation]
        COV --> EIGEN[Principal Moments Analysis]
        EIGEN --> WEIGHTS[Shape Weight Computation]
        WEIGHTS --> COORDS[Triangular Coordinates]
        COORDS --> PLOT[ImPlot Visualization]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Components"
        SHAPESPACE[Shapespace Event Handler]
        ARENA[Arena Allocator]
        TASK_SYS[Task System]
        EXPORT[Export System]
    end
    
    SHAPESPACE --> ARENA
    SHAPESPACE --> TASK_SYS
    SHAPESPACE --> EXPORT
    TASK --> TASK_SYS
    PLOT --> SHAPESPACE
```

**Shape Space Triangle Coordinate System**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Triangular Shape Space"
        LINEAR["Linear (0,0)"]
        PLANAR["Planar (1,0)"] 
        SPHERICAL["Spherical (0.5, 0.866)"]
        
        LINEAR -.-> PLANAR
        PLANAR -.-> SPHERICAL  
        SPHERICAL -.-> LINEAR
    end
    
    subgraph "Shape Weight Computation"
        LAMBDA1[λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃] --> NORM[Normalize Eigenvalues]
        NORM --> W1[w_linear = λ₁ - λ₂]
        NORM --> W2[w_planar = λ₂ - λ₃] 
        NORM --> W3[w_spherical = λ₃]
        W1 --> COORDS[Barycentric Coordinates]
        W2 --> COORDS
        W3 --> COORDS
    end
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:1-503]()

## Core Architecture

### Main Component Structure

The `Shapespace` struct serves as the primary component, inheriting from `viamd::EventHandler` to integrate with the event system:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Shapespace {
        +char input[256]
        +char error[256]
        +bool input_valid
        +bool show_window

        +size_t num_frames
        +size_t num_structures
        +md_array(vec3_t) weights
        +md_array(vec2_t) coords
        +md_array(md_bitfield_t) bitfields
        +md_bitfield_t joined_bitfield
        +md_allocator_i* arena
        +float marker_size
        +bool use_mass
        +ColorMode mode
        +task_system::ID evaluate_task
        +ApplicationState* app_state
        +process_events()
        +draw_window()
        +export_shape_space()
    }

        <<interface>>
        +process_events()
    }

```

The component maintains arrays for shape weights (`vec3_t`), 2D plot coordinates (`vec2_t`), and atom selection bitfields for each analyzed structure.

## Shape Computation Algorithm

### Parallel Frame Processing

The core computation is parallelized across trajectory frames using the task system:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Frame Processing Pipeline"
        FRAME[Frame Data] --> COORDS[Extract Coordinates]
        COORDS --> FILTER[Apply Atom Filter]
        FILTER --> COM[Compute Center of Mass]
        COM --> DEPERIODIZE[Deperiodize Coordinates]
        DEPERIODIZE --> COV[Covariance Matrix]
        COV --> EIGEN[Principal Moments]
        EIGEN --> NORMALIZE[Shape Weights]
        NORMALIZE --> BARY[Barycentric Coords]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Execution"
        TASK1[Thread 1: Frames 0-N/4]
        TASK2[Thread 2: Frames N/4-N/2]
        TASK3[Thread 3: Frames N/2-3N/4]
        TASK4[Thread 4: Frames 3N/4-N]
    end
```

The computation occurs in the lambda function passed to `task_system::create_pool_task()`:

- Allocates thread-local coordinate arrays
- Iterates through assigned frame range
- Loads frame coordinates using `md_trajectory_load_frame()`
- Processes each structure's atom selection
- Computes center of mass with `md_util_com_compute_vec4()`
- Calculates covariance matrix with `mat3_covariance_matrix_vec4()`
- Derives shape weights using `md_util_shape_weights()`

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-426]()

### Mathematical Foundation

The shape analysis is based on the eigenvalue decomposition of the covariance matrix:

1. **Covariance Matrix**: Computed from deperiodized atomic coordinates
2. **Eigenvalues**: Ordered as λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃  
3. **Shape Weights**: 
   - Linear: λ₁ - λ₂ (elongation along primary axis)
   - Planar: λ₂ - λ₃ (flattening in secondary plane) 
   - Spherical: λ₃ (isotropic distribution)
4. **Normalization**: Weights sum to 1.0
5. **Triangular Coordinates**: Barycentric mapping to triangle vertices

The triangular coordinate system maps shape weights to visualization coordinates:
```
p[0] = {0.0f, 0.0f}         // Linear vertex
p[1] = {1.0f, 0.0f}         // Planar vertex  
p[2] = {0.5f, 0.86602540378f} // Spherical vertex (equilateral triangle)
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:394-422]()

## Memory Management

The component uses arena allocation for efficient memory management:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Memory Layout"
        ARENA[Arena Allocator] --> BITFIELDS[Structure Bitfields]
        ARENA --> WEIGHTS[Shape Weights Array]
        ARENA --> COORDS[Plot Coordinates Array]
        ARENA --> JOINED[Joined Bitfield]
    end
    
    subgraph "Lifecycle"
        INIT[Initialize] --> ALLOCATE[Allocate Arrays]
        ALLOCATE --> RESET[Reset on Re-evaluation]
        RESET --> DEALLOCATE[Cleanup on Shutdown]
    end
```

Memory allocation strategy:
- **Arena Size**: 1 MB allocated from persistent allocator
- **Array Sizing**: `num_frames * num_structures` elements
- **Reset Strategy**: Arena reset on filter expression changes
- **Thread Safety**: Separate heap allocations for worker threads

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:82-84](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:354-356](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:387-388]()

## Integration Points

### Filter System Integration

The component integrates with the molecular filter system to define atom selections:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Filter Processing"
        INPUT[User Filter Expression] --> PARSE[md_filter_evaluate]
        PARSE --> VALIDATE[Input Validation]

    end
```

Filter evaluation produces bitfields for each structure that define which atoms participate in the shape analysis.

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:360-376]()

### Task System Integration

The component leverages the task system for parallel computation across trajectory frames:

- **Task Creation**: `task_system::create_pool_task()` with frame-based parallelization
- **Task Management**: Interrupt running tasks on parameter changes
- **Thread Safety**: Each worker thread allocates separate coordinate arrays
- **Synchronization**: Task completion updates UI state

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:346-348](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-427]()

# Shape Space Analysis

## Purpose and Scope

The Shape Space Analysis component provides real-time computation and visualization of molecular shape descriptors for trajectory analysis. It computes principal moments of inertia for selected atoms across trajectory frames and plots the resulting shape weights in a triangular coordinate system that represents the spectrum from linear to planar to spherical molecular conformations.

For general analysis and computation framework information, see [Analysis and Computation](#4). For parallel processing details used by this component, see [Task System and Parallel Processing](#4.1).

## Overview

The Shape Space Analysis system analyzes molecular shapes by computing three normalized shape weights (linear, planar, and isotropic) based on the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of atomic coordinates. These weights are visualized in a triangular plot where the vertices represent idealized linear, planar, and spherical shapes.

**Shape Space Analysis Workflow**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Shape Space Analysis Workflow"
        INPUT["User Filter Expression"] --> PARSE["md_filter_evaluate"]
        PARSE --> BITFIELDS["Atom Selection Bitfields"]
        BITFIELDS --> TASK["Parallel Frame Processing"]
        TASK --> COM["Center of Mass Computation"]
        COM --> COV["Covariance Matrix Calculation"]
        COV --> EIGEN["Principal Moments Analysis"]
        EIGEN --> WEIGHTS["Shape Weight Computation"]
        WEIGHTS --> COORDS["Triangular Coordinates"]
        COORDS --> PLOT["ImPlot Visualization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Components"
        SHAPESPACE["Shapespace Event Handler"]
        ARENA["Arena Allocator"]
        TASK_SYS["Task System"]
        EXPORT["Export System"]
    end
    
    SHAPESPACE --> ARENA
    SHAPESPACE --> TASK_SYS
    SHAPESPACE --> EXPORT
    TASK --> TASK_SYS
    PLOT --> SHAPESPACE
```

**Shape Space Triangle Coordinate System**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Triangular Shape Space"
        LINEAR["Linear (0,0)"]
        PLANAR["Planar (1,0)"] 
        SPHERICAL["Spherical (0.5, 0.866)"]
        
        LINEAR -.-> PLANAR
        PLANAR -.-> SPHERICAL  
        SPHERICAL -.-> LINEAR
    end
    
    subgraph "Shape Weight Computation"
        LAMBDA1["λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃"] --> NORM["Normalize Eigenvalues"]
        NORM --> W1["w_linear = λ₁ - λ₂"]
        NORM --> W2["w_planar = λ₂ - λ₃"] 
        NORM --> W3["w_spherical = λ₃"]
        W1 --> COORDS["Barycentric Coordinates"]
        W2 --> COORDS
        W3 --> COORDS
    end
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:1-503]()

## Core Architecture

### Main Component Structure

The `Shapespace` struct serves as the primary component, inheriting from `viamd::EventHandler` to integrate with the event system:

**Shapespace Component Architecture**
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Shapespace {
        +char input[256]
        +char error[256]
        +bool input_valid
        +bool show_window
        +uint64_t eval_hash
        +size_t num_frames
        +size_t num_structures
        +md_array_vec3_t weights
        +md_array_vec2_t coords
        +md_array_md_bitfield_t bitfields
        +md_bitfield_t joined_bitfield
        +md_allocator_i arena
        +float marker_size
        +bool use_mass
        +ColorMode mode
        +task_system_ID evaluate_task
        +ApplicationState app_state
        +process_events()
        +draw_window()
        +export_shape_space()
    }
    
    class EventHandler {
        <<interface>>
        +process_events()
    }
    
    Shapespace --|> EventHandler
```

The component maintains arrays for shape weights (`vec3_t`), 2D plot coordinates (`vec2_t`), and atom selection bitfields for each analyzed structure.

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:42-74]()

### Event System Integration

The component responds to key application events through the event system:

| Event Type | Handler Function | Purpose |
|------------|------------------|---------|
| `ViamdInitialize` | Initialize arena allocator | Setup memory management |
| `ViamdShutdown` | Cleanup and task interruption | Resource cleanup |
| `ViamdFrameTick` | `draw_window()` | Update UI and trigger evaluation |
| `ViamdWindowDrawMenu` | Menu checkbox | Window visibility control |
| `ViamdSerialize/Deserialize` | State persistence | Save/load configuration |

**Event Processing Sequence**
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as "Application"
    participant Event as "Event System"
    participant Shape as "Shapespace"
    participant Task as "Task System"
    
    App->>Event: ViamdInitialize
    Event->>Shape: process_events()
    Shape->>Shape: Initialize arena allocator
    
    App->>Event: ViamdFrameTick
    Event->>Shape: process_events()
    Shape->>Shape: draw_window()
    Shape->>Shape: Check eval_hash
    
    alt Hash changed
        Shape->>Task: create_pool_task()
        Shape->>Task: enqueue_task()
    end
    
    App->>Event: ViamdShutdown
    Event->>Shape: process_events()
    Shape->>Task: task_interrupt_and_wait_for()
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:76-127]()

## Shape Computation Algorithm

### Parallel Frame Processing

The core computation is parallelized across trajectory frames using the task system:

**Frame Processing Pipeline**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Frame Processing Pipeline"
        FRAME["Frame Data"] --> COORDS["Extract Coordinates"]
        COORDS --> FILTER["Apply Atom Filter"]
        FILTER --> COM["Compute Center of Mass"]
        COM --> DEPERIODIZE["Deperiodize Coordinates"]
        DEPERIODIZE --> COV["Covariance Matrix"]
        COV --> EIGEN["Principal Moments"]
        EIGEN --> NORMALIZE["Shape Weights"]
        NORMALIZE --> BARY["Barycentric Coords"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Execution"
        TASK1["Thread 1: Frames 0-N/4"]
        TASK2["Thread 2: Frames N/4-N/2"]
        TASK3["Thread 3: Frames N/2-3N/4"]
        TASK4["Thread 4: Frames 3N/4-N"]
    end
```

The computation occurs in the lambda function passed to `task_system::create_pool_task()`:

- Allocates thread-local coordinate arrays
- Iterates through assigned frame range
- Loads frame coordinates using `md_trajectory_load_frame()`
- Processes each structure's atom selection
- Computes center of mass with `md_util_com_compute_vec4()`
- Calculates covariance matrix with `mat3_covariance_matrix_vec4()`
- Derives shape weights using `md_util_shape_weights()`

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-426]()

### Mathematical Foundation

The shape analysis is based on the eigenvalue decomposition of the covariance matrix:

1. **Covariance Matrix**: Computed from deperiodized atomic coordinates
2. **Eigenvalues**: Ordered as λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃  
3. **Shape Weights**: 
   - Linear: λ₁ - λ₂ (elongation along primary axis)
   - Planar: λ₂ - λ₃ (flattening in secondary plane) 
   - Spherical: λ₃ (isotropic distribution)
4. **Normalization**: Weights sum to 1.0
5. **Triangular Coordinates**: Barycentric mapping to triangle vertices

The triangular coordinate system maps shape weights to visualization coordinates:
```
p[0] = {0.0f, 0.0f}         // Linear vertex
p[1] = {1.0f, 0.0f}         // Planar vertex  
p[2] = {0.5f, 0.86602540378f} // Spherical vertex (equilateral triangle)
```

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:394-422]()

## Memory Management

The component uses arena allocation for efficient memory management:

**Memory Management Architecture**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Memory Layout"
        ARENA["Arena Allocator"] --> BITFIELDS["Structure Bitfields"]
        ARENA --> WEIGHTS["Shape Weights Array"]
        ARENA --> COORDS["Plot Coordinates Array"]
        ARENA --> JOINED["Joined Bitfield"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Lifecycle"
        INIT["Initialize"] --> ALLOCATE["Allocate Arrays"]
        ALLOCATE --> RESET["Reset on Re-evaluation"]
        RESET --> DEALLOCATE["Cleanup on Shutdown"]
    end
```

Memory allocation strategy:
- **Arena Size**: 1 MB allocated from persistent allocator
- **Array Sizing**: `num_frames * num_structures` elements
- **Reset Strategy**: Arena reset on filter expression changes
- **Thread Safety**: Separate heap allocations for worker threads

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:82-84](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:354-356](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:387-388]()

## Integration Points

### Filter System Integration

The component integrates with the molecular filter system to define atom selections:

**Filter System Integration**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Filter Processing"
        INPUT["User Filter Expression"] --> PARSE["md_filter_evaluate"]
        PARSE --> VALIDATE["Input Validation"]
        VALIDATE --> BITFIELDS["Generate Bitfields"]
        BITFIELDS --> JOIN["Create Joined Bitfield"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Error Handling"
        ERROR["Parse Error"] --> DISPLAY["Show Error Tooltip"]
        VALID["Valid Input"] --> HIGHLIGHT["Update Highlight Mask"]
    end
```

Filter evaluation produces bitfields for each structure that define which atoms participate in the shape analysis.

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:360-376]()

### Task System Integration

The component leverages the task system for parallel computation across trajectory frames:

- **Task Creation**: `task_system::create_pool_task()` with frame-based parallelization
- **Task Management**: Interrupt running tasks on parameter changes
- **Thread Safety**: Each worker thread allocates separate coordinate arrays
- **Synchronization**: Task completion updates UI state

Sources: [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:346-348](), [src/components/shapespace/shapespace.cpp:382-427]()

# Page: VeloxChem Integration

# VeloxChem Integration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp](src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp)
- [src/main.cpp](src/main.cpp)
- [src/viamd.h](src/viamd.h)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The VeloxChem Integration system provides comprehensive support for loading, processing, and visualizing quantum chemistry data from VeloxChem calculations within VIAMD. This integration enables users to analyze molecular orbitals, natural transition orbitals, electron densities, response properties, and vibrational modes through both 2D plots and 3D volume visualizations.

For information about the general visualization pipeline, see [Graphics and Visualization Pipeline](#3). For details about the task system used for computational work, see [Task System and Parallel Processing](#4.1).

## System Architecture

The VeloxChem integration is implemented as an event-driven component that responds to application lifecycle events and representation evaluation requests. The system supports both CPU and GPU computation paths for quantum mechanical function evaluation.

### Core Component Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "VeloxChem Component"
        VLX_HANDLER["VeloxChem Event Handler<br/>veloxchem.cpp"]
        VLX_DATA["md_vlx_t<br/>VeloxChem Data Parser"]
        ARENA["Memory Arena<br/>Persistent Allocations"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Computation Modules"
        ORB_MOD["Orbital Module<br/>Molecular Orbital Analysis"]
        NTO_MOD["NTO Module<br/>Natural Transition Orbitals"]
        RSP_MOD["Response Module<br/>UV-Vis/ECD Spectra"]
        VIB_MOD["Vibrational Module<br/>IR Spectra & Modes"]
        OPT_MOD["Optimization Module<br/>Geometry Optimization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Computation Engines"
        GPU_PATH["GPU Compute Path<br/>compute_*_GPU()"]
        CPU_PATH["CPU Async Path<br/>compute_*_async()"]
        GTO_EVAL["GTO Evaluation<br/>md_gto_*"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        VOLUME_VIS["Volume Rendering<br/>3D Electronic Structure"]
        PLOT_VIS["2D Plotting<br/>Spectra & Analysis"]
        ISO_SURF["Isosurface Rendering<br/>Orbital Visualization"]
    end
    
    VLX_HANDLER --> VLX_DATA
    VLX_HANDLER --> ARENA
    
    VLX_HANDLER --> ORB_MOD
    VLX_HANDLER --> NTO_MOD
    VLX_HANDLER --> RSP_MOD
    VLX_HANDLER --> VIB_MOD
    VLX_HANDLER --> OPT_MOD
    
    ORB_MOD --> GPU_PATH
    ORB_MOD --> CPU_PATH
    NTO_MOD --> GPU_PATH
    NTO_MOD --> CPU_PATH
    
    GPU_PATH --> GTO_EVAL
    CPU_PATH --> GTO_EVAL
    
    GTO_EVAL --> VOLUME_VIS
    VOLUME_VIS --> ISO_SURF
    RSP_MOD --> PLOT_VIS
    VIB_MOD --> PLOT_VIS
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:288-803](), [src/viamd.h:105-128]()

## Data Structures and File Parsing

### VeloxChem Data Container

The core data structure `md_vlx_t` encapsulates all quantum chemistry data parsed from VeloxChem output files. The integration supports both text-based `.out` files and HDF5 `.h5` files.

Key data accessed through the VeloxChem API includes:
- **Molecular orbital coefficients and energies**: `md_vlx_scf_mo_energy()`, `md_vlx_scf_mo_occupancy()`
- **Natural transition orbital data**: `md_vlx_rsp_nto_lambdas()`, `md_vlx_nto_gto_extract()`
- **Response properties**: `md_vlx_rsp_absorption_ev()`, `md_vlx_rsp_electric_transition_dipole_moments()`
- **Atomic properties**: `md_vlx_scf_resp_charges()`, `md_vlx_atomic_numbers()`

### Orbital Bounding Volume Computation

The system computes oriented bounding boxes (OBB) and axis-aligned bounding boxes (AABB) to optimize volume rendering of electronic structure data:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ATOMS["Atomic Coordinates<br/>md_vlx_atom_coordinates()"]
    PCA["Principal Component Analysis<br/>mat3_covariance_matrix_vec4()"]
    OBB["Oriented Bounding Box<br/>obb.orientation, obb.min_ext, obb.max_ext"]
    AABB["Axis-Aligned Bounding Box<br/>aabb.min_ext, aabb.max_ext"]
    GRID["Volume Grid<br/>md_grid_t with optimal dimensions"]
    
    ATOMS --> PCA
    PCA --> OBB
    ATOMS --> AABB
    OBB --> GRID
    AABB --> GRID
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:849-898]()

## Computational Modules

### Molecular Orbital Analysis

The orbital module handles visualization and analysis of molecular orbitals with support for both alpha and beta spin orbitals.

#### Orbital Types and Evaluation Modes

| Electronic Structure Type | Evaluation Mode | GPU Function | CPU Function |
|---------------------------|-----------------|--------------|---------------|
| Molecular Orbital (Ψ) | `MD_GTO_EVAL_MODE_PSI` | `compute_mo_GPU()` | `compute_mo_async()` |
| Molecular Orbital Density (Ψ²) | `MD_GTO_EVAL_MODE_PSI_SQUARED` | `compute_mo_GPU()` | `compute_mo_async()` |
| Electron Density (ρ) | `MD_GTO_EVAL_MODE_PSI_SQUARED` | `compute_electron_density_GPU()` | `compute_electron_density_async()` |

#### HOMO/LUMO Detection

The system automatically identifies HOMO and LUMO indices for both alpha and beta electrons:

```cpp
homo_idx[0] = (int)md_vlx_scf_homo_idx(vlx, MD_VLX_MO_TYPE_ALPHA);
lumo_idx[0] = (int)md_vlx_scf_lumo_idx(vlx, MD_VLX_MO_TYPE_ALPHA);
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:837-841](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:1264-1403]()

### Natural Transition Orbital (NTO) Analysis

NTO analysis provides insight into electronic excitations by computing particle and hole densities, attachment/detachment densities, and transition matrices.

#### NTO Data Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    EXCITED_STATES["Excited States<br/>md_vlx_rsp_number_of_excited_states()"]
    LAMBDAS["Lambda Values<br/>md_vlx_rsp_nto_lambdas()"]
    PARTICLE["Particle Orbitals<br/>MD_VLX_NTO_TYPE_PARTICLE"]
    HOLE["Hole Orbitals<br/>MD_VLX_NTO_TYPE_HOLE"]
    ATTACH["Attachment Density<br/>AttachmentDetachmentType::Attachment"]
    DETACH["Detachment Density<br/>AttachmentDetachmentType::Detachment"]
    DIPOLES["Transition Dipoles<br/>md_vlx_rsp_electric_transition_dipole_moments()"]
    
    EXCITED_STATES --> LAMBDAS
    LAMBDAS --> PARTICLE
    LAMBDAS --> HOLE
    PARTICLE --> ATTACH
    HOLE --> DETACH
    EXCITED_STATES --> DIPOLES
```

#### Group-Based Analysis

The NTO module supports molecular fragment analysis through group assignments:

```cpp
nto.atom_group_idx = (uint32_t*)md_alloc(arena, sizeof(uint32_t) * mol.atom.count);
nto.group.count = 3;
for (size_t i = 0; i < mol.atom.count; ++i) {
    nto.atom_group_idx[i] = i < mol.atom.count / 2 ? 1 : 2;
}
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:900-955](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:1038-1082]()

### Response Property Analysis

The response module handles UV-Vis absorption and ECD (Electronic Circular Dichroism) spectra computation with configurable broadening functions.

#### Spectral Broadening

| Broadening Type | Mathematical Form | Use Case |
|----------------|-------------------|----------|
| Gaussian | `exp(-(x-x₀)²/(2σ²))` | Natural line shapes |
| Lorentzian | `γ/((x-x₀)² + γ²)` | Lifetime broadening |

#### Response Data Processing

```mermaid
graph LR
    RAW_DATA["Raw Transition Data<br/>Energy, Oscillator Strength"]
    BROADENING["Spectral Broadening<br/>Gaussian/Lorentzian"]
    UNIT_CONV["Unit Conversion<br/>eV, nm, cm⁻¹, hartree"]
    PLOT_DATA["Plot Arrays<br/>x_ev_samples[], eps[], ecd[]"]
    
    RAW_DATA --> BROADENING
    BROADENING --> UNIT_CONV
    UNIT_CONV --> PLOT_DATA
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:958-976](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:93-110]()

## Volume Computation Pipeline

### GPU vs CPU Computation Paths

The system automatically selects between GPU and CPU computation based on OpenGL capability detection:

```cpp
use_gpu_path = (!FORCE_CPU_PATH && gl_major >= 4 && gl_minor >= 3);
```

#### GPU Computation Path

```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT["Input Parameters<br/>Grid, Orbital Index, Mode"]
    EXTRACT["Extract GTOs<br/>md_vlx_mo_gto_extract()"]
    FILTER["Apply Cutoff Filter<br/>md_gto_cutoff_compute_and_filter()"]
    COMPUTE["GPU Evaluation<br/>md_gto_grid_evaluate_GPU()"]
    OUTPUT["Volume Texture<br/>GL_R32F Format"]
    
    INPUT --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> FILTER
    FILTER --> COMPUTE
    COMPUTE --> OUTPUT
```

#### CPU Async Computation Path

```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT["Input Parameters<br/>Grid, Orbital Data"]
    ARENA["Allocate Memory Arena<br/>md_vm_arena_create()"]
    TASK["Create Pool Task<br/>evaluate_gto_on_grid_async()"]
    MAIN_TASK["Create Main Task<br/>Update Texture"]
    DEPENDENCY["Set Task Dependency<br/>task_system::set_task_dependency()"]
    
    INPUT --> ARENA
    ARENA --> TASK
    TASK --> MAIN_TASK
    MAIN_TASK --> DEPENDENCY
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:513-517](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:1264-1403]()

### Grid Generation and Volume Initialization

The system computes optimal grid dimensions based on molecular geometry and desired resolution:

```cpp
static inline void compute_dim(int out_dim[3], const vec3_t& in_ext, float samples_per_unit_length) {
    out_dim[0] = CLAMP(ALIGN_TO((int)(in_ext.x * samples_per_unit_length), 8), 8, 512);
    out_dim[1] = CLAMP(ALIGN_TO((int)(in_ext.y * samples_per_unit_length), 8), 8, 512);
    out_dim[2] = CLAMP(ALIGN_TO((int)(in_ext.z * samples_per_unit_length), 8), 8, 512);
}
```

Volume resolution settings map to different sampling densities:

| Resolution | Samples per Ångström | Typical Grid Size |
|------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Low | 4.0 | 64³ to 128³ |
| Mid | 8.0 | 128³ to 256³ |
| High | 16.0 | 256³ to 512³ |

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:224-228](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:1000-1018]()

## Integration with Representation System

### Atom Property Integration

The component provides atomic properties like RESP charges through the `RepresentationEvalAtomProperty` event:

```cpp
case ATOM_PROPERTY_RESP_CHARGE: {
    const double* resp_charges = md_vlx_scf_resp_charges(vlx);
    if (resp_charges) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < num_atoms; ++i) {
            data.dst_values[i] = (float)resp_charges[i];
        }
        data.output_written = true;
    }
    break;
}
```

## User Interface Components

### Analysis Windows

The VeloxChem integration provides several specialized analysis windows accessible through the main menu:

| Window | Purpose | Key Functions |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| Summary | Overview of quantum data | Basic molecular information |
| Response | UV-Vis/ECD spectra | Spectral analysis and export |
| Orbital Grid | Molecular orbital visualization | Interactive orbital browser |
| Transition Analysis | NTO analysis | Excitation analysis and dipoles |
| Export | Volume data export | High-resolution orbital export |

### Orbital Grid Interface

The orbital grid provides an interactive browser for molecular orbitals with configurable layout:

```cpp
struct Orb {
    Volume   vol[16] = {};
    int      vol_mo_idx[16] = {-1,-1,...};
    uint32_t iso_tex[16] = {};
    int num_x = 3;
    int num_y = 3;
    int mo_idx = -1;
};
```

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:535-545](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:319-350]()

## Memory Management and Performance

### Arena-Based Allocation

The VeloxChem component uses arena-based memory management for efficient handling of large quantum chemistry datasets:

```cpp
arena = md_arena_allocator_create(state.allocator.persistent, MEGABYTES(4));
```

### Asynchronous Task Management

Large volume computations are handled asynchronously using the task system to prevent UI blocking:

```mermaid
graph TD
    TASK_CREATE["Create Pool Task<br/>task_system::create_pool_task()"]
    ASYNC_EVAL["Async Grid Evaluation<br/>evaluate_gto_on_grid_async()"]
    MAIN_UPDATE["Main Thread Update<br/>gl::set_texture_3D_data()"]
    CLEANUP["Memory Cleanup<br/>md_vm_arena_destroy()"]
    
    TASK_CREATE --> ASYNC_EVAL
    ASYNC_EVAL --> MAIN_UPDATE
    MAIN_UPDATE --> CLEANUP
```

### Performance Optimizations

- **GTO Cutoff Filtering**: Eliminates negligible basis functions using `md_gto_cutoff_compute_and_filter()`
- **Grid Alignment**: Ensures optimal memory access patterns with 8-byte alignment
- **GPU Memory Management**: Direct texture updates without CPU roundtrips for GPU path
- **Incremental Updates**: Only recomputes volumes when orbital indices change

Sources: [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:512](), [src/components/veloxchem/veloxchem.cpp:1351-1403]()
